name: Ghostbuster Detection
description: Applies Ghostbuster method combining multiple weak signals — structured search over feature combinations (Verma et al., 2023).
mechanism:
The Ghostbuster Detection method implements the technique from Verma et al. (2023) for detecting AI-generated text using structured search over weaker language models:

1. **Feature Vector Construction**: The input text is processed through a series of weaker, unstructured language models (e.g., unigram, bigram, trigram models and a small GPT-like model). For each token, the probability assigned by each model is computed, yielding per-token probability vectors from multiple model perspectives.

2. **Document-Level Feature Aggregation**: Token-level probabilities are aggregated into document-level features using selected functions: mean, variance, and quantile statistics of log-probabilities from each model. This creates a compact feature vector capturing the distributional characteristics of the text through multiple linguistic lenses.

3. **Structured Search over Feature Combinations**: A structured search selects the most discriminative combination of features and models. Rather than relying on a single powerful model, Ghostbuster combines signals from multiple weaker models — exploiting the observation that AI-generated text exhibits characteristic probability patterns across different model architectures.

4. **Linear Classification**: The selected feature vector is fed into a trained logistic regression classifier. The linear model ensures interpretability and robustness — avoiding overfitting to specific generator architectures. The decision boundary separates human-written text (which shows variable probability across models) from AI-generated text (which tends to be uniformly probable across models).

5. **Confidence Scoring**: The classifier output probability provides a confidence score. Texts near the decision boundary are flagged as uncertain, while those with strong signals from multiple feature dimensions receive high-confidence predictions. The method generalizes across different AI generators without requiring per-model training.
parameters: Analysis type: automated statistical\nScore range: 0 (authentic) to 100 (AI-generated)\nMinimum input size: varies by media type
accuracy: Moderate to High — 70-85% accuracy depending on input quality and method combination.
source: Based on peer-reviewed research in digital forensics and AI content detection.
useCase: Used as part of multi-signal analysis pipeline to detect AI-generated content.
strengths:
• Research-backed methodology
• Fast computation time
• Complementary to other detection methods
• Works across different AI generators
limitations: • Accuracy varies with input quality\n• Best used in combination with other methods\n• May require calibration for new AI models
